data.title: Structure and function of TM6SF1 reveals role in mTORC1 signaling
data.authors: Hong S; Li X et al.
data.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Cryo-EM structure of TM6SF1 identifies it as a lysosomal cholesterol-binding protein that directly engages LAMTOR1 (Ragulator) to regulate mTORC1 signaling in a cholesterol-dependent manner.
data.abstract_excerpt: The transmembrane 6 superfamily (TM6SF) comprises two members: TM6SF1, a ubiquitously expressed lysosomal membrane protein of unknown function, and TM6SF2, an endoplasmic reticulum protein required for bulk lipidation of Apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins. Here, we used cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to determine the structure of human TM6SF1 at 2.9-Å resolution. TM6SF1 forms a polytopic homodimer, with each protomer comprising 10 transmembrane helices (TMs). TMs 1-6 form a pocket that accommodates a cholesterol molecule.

extracted_findings.effect: Loss of TM6SF1 reduces mTORC1 signaling (S6K1/4E-BP1 phosphorylation) and activates TFEB, in a cholesterol-dependent manner
